A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ADCL/EGSR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original Qwen2.5-7B benchmark results, curriculum and perplexity analyses, pass@32 evaluations, and a reasoning case study.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, alongside additional training diagnostics.

M1.justification: The ADCL batch re-ranking procedure and EGSR guided-trajectory replacement remain unchanged. Equations 1–4 and Algorithms 1–2 match; the condensed method descriptions and additional model evaluations do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use BaseSet-7K and AugSet-10K derived from S1 and DeepScaleR, and evaluate mathematical reasoning on MATH-500, AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, and Minervamath. The shortened MATH table heading does not indicate a different dataset. Additional model configurations do not extend task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding Qwen2.5-7B comparisons retain the same comparator membership, including SFT, standard RL, PCL, and direct off-policy replacement. The added model evaluations and training plots reuse existing comparison strategies rather than introduce new baseline methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Table 2 extend evaluation from Qwen2.5-7B to Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct across four retained benchmarks. This substantially expands the tested model scales and families. Table 2 specifies the same experimental setup as Table 1; the original benchmark metrics and data construction remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit testing of generalization across model families and scales, plus EGSR versus RL/off-policy reward dynamics and SFT optimization diagnostics in Figures 5–6. The original perplexity, pass@32, and reasoning-case analyses remain. The NIR analysis moves to Appendix D, while Figure 4 largely redisplays existing ADCL curves.

E5.justification: The existing perplexity distributions and rank-deviation quantiles are retained. V2 adds no reported seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures; its additional training traces do not specify a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds substantial results for two model configurations: combined ADCL/EGSR obtains MATH scores of 69.80 versus RL's 59.00 on Qwen2.5-1.5B, and 60.60 versus 53.20 on Llama3.1-8B-Instruct. Figures 5–6 add training outcomes. All numerical entries in the original Tables 1 and 3 and the relocated NIR table are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the mathematical reasoning in the retained case study are unchanged. The new educational-psychology motivation introduces no formal assumptions, mathematical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The first contribution changes from theoretical insights about human learning mechanisms to conceptual and empirical insights identifying Difficulty Shift and supporting stable expert-knowledge integration. The central ADCL/EGSR contributions and the headline AIME24 and AIME25 improvement claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning fixed re-estimation frequency, dependence on expert-demonstration quality, and untested training paradigms and domains. It introduces ZPD and self-explanation interpretations and interprets Table 2 as evidence of broader model applicability. Conversely, it removes the detailed explanation that gradual post-training shifts make local re-ranking preferable to full-dataset SPL.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies SFT's learning rate of 2e-5 with decay, maximum length of 8192, and gradient accumulation of 1. It separately assigns gradient accumulation of 4 to GRPO. These clarify previously underspecified SFT settings without establishing that the original experiment was rerun.

R1.justification: V2 grounds the human-learning motivation in Vygotsky and Cole's ZPD and Chi et al.'s self-explanation work, replacing the informal exercise-book analogy. It also adds the Llama and Qwen model-report citations. The broader positioning against static curricula and direct off-policy learning remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially streamlines the introduction, related work, method exposition, and conclusion, including replacing ADCL's numbered explanation with prose and removing duplicated perplexity discussion. It reorganizes the analysis section, moves NIR discussion into Appendix D, and adds a dedicated limitations section.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-model Table 2 and Figures 4–6, expands the hyperparameter table, and relocates the NIR table to Appendix D. Figures 1–3 retain identical graphics, while Figure 4 redisplays ADCL dynamics. The later appendices switch from full-width presentation to two-column layouts, substantially reflowing prompts and the case study.

improvement.justification: V1's evidence for broadly useful training strategies depended on one Qwen2.5-7B backbone. V2 substantially strengthens that evidence by testing a smaller Qwen model and a different Llama family with the existing comparison strategies, demonstrating combined-method gains over RL across four retained benchmarks. SFT settings, training diagnostics, and specific limitations also improve transparency. Some explanatory detail is lost, and mathematical-domain scope and absent run-level uncertainty remain limitations, but these do not outweigh the stronger empirical support.
